limitations: Two John Gurney apprentices exist (glover's son of 'Moborne', Worcestershire, bound 1602; Aylesbury ironmonger's son, bound 1655) but neither fits the emigrant's chronology or parentage.

The dataset covers the Merchant Taylors' Company only; a John trained in another London livery (Drapers, Clothworkers, Worsted Weavers), in a country apprenticeship off the London books, or informally within a household would not appear.
Absence of a patrimony freedom does not by itself disprove the Candidate-B parentage; it removes a supporting inference the case file had not explicitly claimed.

finding.shortLabel: No Merchant Taylors' binding or patrimony freedom for John

sources.locator: UKDA-SN-9263 (Scott 2024), all five sheets; Gurney-variant filter (47 occurrences); John bindings vol.3b no.852 (Worcs. glover's son, 1602) and vol.14 no.514 (Aylesbury ironmonger's son, 1655); Patrimony sheet 3,391 rows, zero Gurney

finding.statement: The Merchant Taylors' Company of London apprentice and freedom records for 1583-1800 (Scott's full transcription of the binding books and freedom registers, UKDA-SN-9263) contain no binding of a John Gurney son of Francis Gurney to any Merchant Taylor master and no Gurney freedom by patrimony at all: the two John Gurney apprentices in the dataset are a glover's son of 'Moborne', Worcestershire (bound 1602) and an Aylesbury ironmonger's son (bound 1655), neither the emigrant, and the 3,391-record patrimony sheet returns zero Gurney variants. The colonial John's tailoring was therefore not transmitted through his proposed father's own livery company, whether by apprenticeship to a fellow Merchant Taylor or by patrimony freedom after Francis Gurney's death.
